body: Topic/author ID inputs are silently "best-effort" here: `find({ id: In(...) })` will drop invalid IDs without telling the caller. Elsewhere (e.g., account interests) the API rejects unknown topic IDs. Consider validating that all provided `dto.topics` (and `dto.authors` / `parentPaperIds`) resolve, and return a 400 when any IDs are invalid to avoid creating Papers with missing associations unexpectedly.

`updateAbstract` / `updateTopics` always return 500 on errors, including the expected "Paper not found" case thrown by `PaperService`. This should map to a 404 (and input validation failures should be 400), otherwise clients can’t distinguish user error from server failure.

These new API helpers return `any` (`paper: any`, `apiRequest<any>`, etc.), which breaks type-safety compared to the rest of this module (which defines concrete response types). Introduce a `Paper` (and maybe `PaperListItem`) type and use it in these request helpers so pages can rely on a stable response shape (especially for `authors`/`topics` being IDs vs objects).

`handleSaveTopics` replaces the entire `paper` state with the response from `updatePaperTopicsRequest`. The current backend implementation of that endpoint returns a Paper loaded with only `topics` relations, so `paper.authors` can become `undefined` after saving and break `isAuthor` checks / author rendering. Either merge the updated topics into the existing `paper` state (instead of replacing it), or ensure the endpoint returns the same fully-populated Paper shape as the initial `getPaperByIdRequest`.

`registerPaper` currently trusts `req.body` without validating required fields (e.g., `title`, `abstractText`, `targetVenue`, and `topics` being a non-empty string/array). Other controllers in this codebase do explicit request-shape validation; adding similar checks here would prevent 500s from DB constraint errors and provide clearer 400 responses to clients.

`paper.authors` is the inverse side of the ManyToMany (the owning side is `User.writtenPapers` which has `@JoinTable()`), so assigning `paper.authors = ...` and then `paperRepo.save(paper)` will not persist the author join rows. Persist the relation from the owning side (e.g., update the selected users' `writtenPapers`), or move the `@JoinTable()` to `Paper.authors` (and remove it from `User.writtenPapers`) so saving the Paper updates the join table.
